decisions.reason: As an updated and positively received version of an already accepted trommel screen, Product A appears to meet or exceed aspiration levels and fits the firm's core mobile screening business.

Product B had a dedicated market presentation at launch and is closely aligned with the firm's established mobile waste-processing portfolio, so with no clear shortfall there is no behavioral trigger to drop it after one year.

Although evidence is still limited, Product C fits the firm's core application areas and a mature machinery producer with some slack would normally keep such a new product on the market until clearer performance feedback arrives.

Product D supports the firm's strategic move toward tougher processing requirements and resource-saving stationary solutions, and the available information does not indicate performance below aspirations severe enough to force withdrawal in 2019.

Product E addresses a specific green-waste niche within the firm's existing customer base, and under bounded rationality the firm would likely continue it while gathering more market feedback rather than redeploy resources immediately.
Product F received its own product-page launch and strongly matches the firm's stationary shredding capabilities, suggesting sufficient strategic and market promise to remain in the portfolio.
